title: Worn fit with over-ear cable
prompt:
USER DESIGN OVERRIDE: retain the compact industrial design in the reference, but CHANGE cable routing to a lower-exit, cable-down configuration. Cable exits the BOTTOM of each earbud and falls below it. No cable over the ear, no upper cable loop, no top cable port. This override takes priority over the reference pixels.
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Input image: the supplied multi-panel concept board is the AUTHORITATIVE product design reference. Match its compact premium in-ear monitor form, not a larger disk-shaped previous design. Use the top-left panel for the complete system, the top-right and bottom-right panels for ear-facing geometry, and bottom-left only for natural ear fit; ignore its over-ear cable routing.
Product identity invariants: compact rounded teardrop/oval shell; smooth subtly domed satin-black outer faceplate with a very thin warm gunmetal/champagne rim (NO radial brushed disc); dark smoked translucent acoustic housing with restrained glimpses of internal structure; short inward-facing acoustic nozzle with a replaceable soft grey silicone tip; a small flexible dark concha wing forming an upper curved hook-like fin integrated into the inner shell; EXACTLY TWO flush pale champagne oval taVNS electrodes located together on the EAR-FACING INNER wing/pad, NOT a metal pad on the extreme tip of the fin. A separate small recessed black-glass rectangular PPG window sits on the ear-facing shell beside the nozzle, containing subtle optical elements; keep this separate from the acoustic bore. Dry EEG contacts are electrically separated conductive areas INTEGRATED INTO THE REPLACEABLE SOFT SILICONE TIP ASSEMBLY, flush with the outer canal-contact surface. They are NOT a separate rigid metallic collar. Appropriate reference/bias contacts remain an engineering decision, not a fixed count in this concept. Black braided cable exits the BOTTOM of the shell through a short downward-pointing dark strain relief and falls naturally below the ear. There is NO over-ear loop and NO top cable connector. The inline controller is a slim rounded charcoal rectangular bar with minus, center and plus buttons and one tiny status light. Its upstream connection is USB-C.
Primary request: an intimate photorealistic macro of a naturally shaped adult ear wearing this compact in-ear monitor, matching the BOTTOM-LEFT panel of the supplied design reference. Warm natural skin texture, dark hair tucked back, cropped temple to upper neck, no full face. The smooth dark oval outer faceplate sits neatly within the lower ear, subtly visible champagne rim, small shell with a natural premium-IEM fit. Inner electrodes and nozzle are concealed where they contact the ear; do not artificially expose them through skin. Soft wing nestles inside the concha, not protruding outside the ear. The braided cable exits the BOTTOM of the earbud and falls STRAIGHT DOWN in front of the ear toward the neck. No cable above or behind the ear, no ear hook. This explicitly overrides the cable route in the supplied reference. Soft daylight, neutral warm grey background, focus on product fit, premium editorial realism. Landscape 4:3, high native detail, whole ear in frame with comfortable margins. No text, no glow, no anatomy graphics, no claims, no markings, no watermarks.
Recovered product-spec constraint: EEG contacts belong to the replaceable soft acoustic-tip assembly, independent of the replaceable two-contact concha wing. PPG is a separate tiny skin-facing window on the INNER housing beside the nozzle, initially in ONE ear. One single acoustic outlet per earpiece; no duplicate hollow port. Most processing and stimulation electronics are in the external controller. Never place the PPG sensor behind the outward faceplate or in the sound path. Do not assert finalized electrode counts or electrical performance.
